worked.title: Q1 · SVM dual: does adding a point raise or lower the optimum?

problem.text: N points, dual SVM: maximise Σαᵢ − ΣᵢΣⱼ αᵢαⱼyᵢyⱼ xᵢ·xⱼ s.t. Σαᵢyᵢ = 0, αᵢ ≥ 0. O_A = optimal value. Add a point (x_{N+1}, y_{N+1}) and solve again: O_B. Which of (a) O_A > O_B, (b) O_A = O_B, (c) O_A < O_B are possible? Justify each.

steps.label: What is tested
steps.text: Comparing two maximisation problems by their feasible sets. The same question is Sep 2024 regular Q(A).

steps.label: Notation
steps.text: This paper's symbols are kept: αᵢ = dual multipliers, O = optimal value of the dual objective. (The paper's objective has no ½; that does not change the argument.)

steps.label: STEP 1 · Old answers still fit the new problem
steps.text:
Take the old optimum α* = (α₁*, …, α_N*) and add α_{N+1} = 0.
Σαᵢyᵢ is unchanged (= 0) and every α ≥ 0 ⇒ it is **feasible** for the new problem.
The new terms all contain α_{N+1} = 0 ⇒ its objective is exactly **O_A**.

steps.label: STEP 2 · So the new maximum is at least O_A
steps.text:
The new problem maximises over a set that contains this point ⇒ **O_B ≥ O_A**.
⇒ **(a) O_A > O_B is impossible.**

steps.label: STEP 3 · (b) O_A = O_B is possible
steps.text: If the new point is correctly classified and outside the margin (y_{N+1}(wᵀx_{N+1} + b) > 1), the old classifier still satisfies every constraint; α_{N+1} = 0 stays optimal and nothing changes.

steps.label: STEP 4 · (c) O_A < O_B is possible
steps.text:
If the new point falls inside the margin or on the wrong side, the old classifier is no longer feasible in the primal. The margin must shrink, ‖w‖ grows, and the optimum (= primal value, by strong duality) goes up.
(If the data stop being separable, the hard-margin dual is unbounded: O_B = +∞.)

steps.label: Answers at a glance
steps.text: (a) impossible; (b) possible (new point outside the margin); (c) possible (new point inside the margin).

steps.label: Where marks are lost
steps.text:
• Arguing only with a picture: the key step is that (α*, 0) is feasible for the new problem.
• Saying "adding data always helps": here the optimum can only go **up**.

steps.label: More
steps.text: Same question: [Lecture 15, Dual tab](#/sem1/aiml-zc416/ch15/f-dual/3).

worked.answer: O_B ≥ O_A always: (a) impossible, (b) and (c) possible.

worked.title: Q4 · SVD when the columns are orthogonal

problem.text: A = [mᵢⱼ] is a full-rank n × n real matrix whose columns are orthogonal. Find its singular value decomposition.

steps.label: What is tested
steps.text: Reading the SVD straight off AᵀA when it is already diagonal.

steps.label: Notation
steps.text: aⱼ = column j of A, dⱼ = ‖aⱼ‖ > 0 (full rank ⇒ no zero column).

steps.label: STEP 1 · AᵀA is diagonal
steps.text:
(AᵀA)ᵢⱼ = aᵢ·aⱼ = 0 for i ≠ j (orthogonal columns)
AᵀA = diag(d₁², …, dₙ²)

steps.label: STEP 2 · V and Σ
steps.text:
AᵀA is already diagonal ⇒ its eigenvectors are the standard basis: **V = I**
σⱼ = √(dⱼ²) = **‖aⱼ‖**: Σ = diag(‖a₁‖, …, ‖aₙ‖)
(Order the columns by decreasing length, i.e. V = a permutation matrix, if σ₁ ≥ σ₂ ≥ … is required.)

steps.label: STEP 3 · U
steps.text:
uⱼ = Avⱼ/σⱼ = aⱼ/‖aⱼ‖: **U = A Σ⁻¹** (the columns of A, each made unit length)
UᵀU = I because the columns are orthonormal ✓

steps.label: STEP 4 · Check
steps.text: UΣVᵀ = AΣ⁻¹ΣI = A ✓

steps.label: Answers at a glance
steps.text: A = UΣVᵀ with U = AΣ⁻¹ (normalised columns), Σ = diag(‖aⱼ‖), V = I (or a permutation to sort σ).

worked.answer: U = columns of A normalised, Σ = diag(column lengths), V = I.

worked.title: Q5 · PCA after a rotation and a shift

problem.text: PCA on x₁, …, x_N gives principal directions b₁, …, b_D. The data become yᵢ = Qxᵢ + μ with QᵀQ = I and μ constant. Find the principal components of the new data in terms of the old ones. How much variance does the first PC capture compared with before?

steps.label: What is tested
steps.text: How the covariance and its eigenvectors change under y = Qx + μ.

steps.label: STEP 1 · The shift disappears
steps.text:
ȳ = Qx̄ + μ ⇒ yᵢ − ȳ = Q(xᵢ − x̄)
PCA works on centred data, so μ has **no effect**.

steps.label: STEP 2 · New covariance
steps.text: S_y = (1/N)Σ Q(xᵢ − x̄)(xᵢ − x̄)ᵀQᵀ = **Q S_x Qᵀ**

steps.label: STEP 3 · New eigenvectors
steps.text:
S_x bⱼ = λⱼbⱼ ⇒ S_y(Qbⱼ) = QS_xQᵀQbⱼ = QS_xbⱼ = λⱼ(Qbⱼ)
So the new principal directions are **Qb₁, …, Qb_D**, with the **same eigenvalues** λⱼ (and they are orthonormal, since Q is).

steps.label: STEP 4 · Variance captured
steps.text: Variance along PC1 = λ₁, unchanged; total = trace(QS_xQᵀ) = trace(S_x), unchanged ⇒ the first PC captures **the same amount and the same fraction** of the variance as before.

steps.label: Answers at a glance
steps.text: New PCs = Qbⱼ; eigenvalues unchanged; μ irrelevant; PC1 captures the same variance (same fraction).

worked.answer: PCs become Qbⱼ; same eigenvalues, so the same variance for PC1.

worked.title: Q6 · Lagrange: maximise a product under a sum-of-squares budget, then AM–GM

problem.text: Maximise the product of the squares of n features, x₁²x₂²⋯xₙ² (n ≥ 2), subject to x₁² + … + xₙ² ≤ c². Formulate and solve. Use the result to prove (a₁a₂⋯aₙ)^{1/n} ≤ (a₁ + … + aₙ)/n for all aᵢ > 0.

steps.label: What is tested
steps.text: Setting up a constrained maximum, solving it with a multiplier, then reading off an inequality.

steps.label: Notation
steps.text: λ = multiplier of the budget constraint (λ ≥ 0, as on the boards). P = x₁²⋯xₙ² (the product).

steps.label: STEP 1 · Formulate
steps.text:
max P = x₁²x₂²⋯xₙ² s.t. x₁² + … + xₙ² − c² ≤ 0
At the maximum the budget is used up (raising any xᵢ² raises P), so the constraint is active: Σxᵢ² = c².

steps.label: STEP 2 · Lagrangian
steps.text: L = x₁²⋯xₙ² − λ(x₁² + … + xₙ² − c²)   (− λg for a maximum)

steps.label: STEP 3 · Stationarity
steps.text:
∂L/∂xₖ = 2P/xₖ − 2λxₖ = 0 ⇒ xₖ² = P/λ for every k
⇒ all xₖ² are **equal**

steps.label: STEP 4 · Solve
steps.text: nxₖ² = c² ⇒ **xₖ² = c²/n** ⇒ max P = **(c²/n)ⁿ**

steps.label: STEP 5 · Prove AM–GM
steps.text:
So for any xᵢ: x₁²⋯xₙ² ≤ ((x₁² + … + xₙ²)/n)ⁿ (take c² = Σxᵢ²).
Put aᵢ = xᵢ² > 0: a₁⋯aₙ ≤ ((a₁ + … + aₙ)/n)ⁿ
Take the n-th root: **(a₁⋯aₙ)^{1/n} ≤ (a₁ + … + aₙ)/n** ∎ (equality when all aᵢ are equal)

steps.label: Answers at a glance
steps.text: xᵢ² = c²/n, maximum (c²/n)ⁿ; with aᵢ = xᵢ² this is the AM–GM inequality.

steps.label: Where marks are lost
steps.text:
• Not explaining why the constraint is active at the maximum.
• Stopping at the maximum without the substitution aᵢ = xᵢ² for the proof.

worked.answer: Max at xᵢ² = c²/n, value (c²/n)ⁿ ⇒ AM–GM.

worked.title: Q7 · Intersection and union of convex sets

problem.text: H₁ and H₂ are convex sets. (a) Prove or disprove that H₁ ∩ H₂ is convex. (b) Prove or disprove that H₁ ∪ H₂ is convex.

steps.label: What is tested
steps.text: The convex-set definition: θx + (1 − θ)y stays in the set.

steps.label: STEP 1 · (a) Intersection: convex
steps.text:
Take x, y ∈ H₁ ∩ H₂ and θ ∈ [0, 1].
x, y ∈ H₁ and H₁ convex ⇒ θx + (1 − θ)y ∈ H₁
x, y ∈ H₂ and H₂ convex ⇒ θx + (1 − θ)y ∈ H₂
⇒ θx + (1 − θ)y ∈ H₁ ∩ H₂ ⇒ **convex** ∎

steps.label: STEP 2 · (b) Union: not convex (counterexample)
steps.text:
H₁ = [0, 1], H₂ = [2, 3] on the real line (both convex).
x = 1 ∈ H₁, y = 2 ∈ H₂, θ = ½: midpoint 1.5 is in neither ⇒ H₁ ∪ H₂ is **not convex** in general.

steps.label: Answers at a glance
steps.text: (a) Always convex. (b) Not always (e.g. [0, 1] ∪ [2, 3]).

steps.label: Where marks are lost
steps.text:
• (b) Saying "false" without a concrete counterexample.
• (a) Using one particular θ instead of a general θ ∈ [0, 1].

steps.label: More
steps.text: Convexity definitions and proofs: [Lecture 11, Convexity tab](#/sem1/aiml-zc416/ch11/f-convex).

worked.title: Q8 · Are b₁ = a₂ − a₃, b₂ = a₁ − a₃, b₃ = a₁ − a₂ independent? (5 marks)

problem.text: a₁, a₂, a₃ ∈ ℝⁿ are linearly independent. b₁ = a₂ − a₃, b₂ = a₁ − a₃, b₃ = a₁ − a₂. Prove or disprove that Q = {b₁, b₂, b₃} is linearly independent. [5M]

steps.label: What is tested
steps.text: Finding a non-trivial combination that gives 0.

steps.label: STEP 1 · Look for a relation
steps.text:
b₁ − b₂ + b₃ = (a₂ − a₃) − (a₁ − a₃) + (a₁ − a₂)
= a₂ − a₃ − a₁ + a₃ + a₁ − a₂ = **0**

steps.label: STEP 2 · Conclude
steps.text:
The coefficients (1, −1, 1) are not all zero ⇒ Q is **linearly dependent**: the claim is **disproved**.
(Equivalently b₂ = b₁ + b₃.)

steps.label: Answers at a glance
steps.text: Dependent: b₁ − b₂ + b₃ = 0.

steps.label: Where marks are lost
steps.text:
• Assuming independence carries over from a₁, a₂, a₃.
• Giving the answer without the explicit combination.

worked.title: Q9 · Quadratic form: matrix, extremum, its type (5 marks)

problem.text: f(x, y, z) = 2x² − 2xy − 4xz + y² + 2yz + 3z² − 2x + 2z. (a) Write f = xᵀAx − bᵀx with A real symmetric. (b) Find the extremum. (c) Minimum, maximum or saddle? [5M]

steps.label: What is tested
steps.text: Building the symmetric matrix of a quadratic, ∇f = 2Ax − b = 0, and the leading-minor test.

steps.label: STEP 1 · (a) A and b
steps.text:
Diagonal = the square terms: 2, 1, 3. Off-diagonal = half of each cross term: xy → −1, xz → −2, yz → 1
**A = [[2, −1, −2], [−1, 1, 1], [−2, 1, 3]]**
−bᵀx = −2x + 2z ⇒ **b = (2, 0, −2)**

steps.label: STEP 4 · (c) Type
steps.text:
Hessian = 2A. Leading minors of A: D₁ = 2 > 0, D₂ = 2·1 − 1 = 1 > 0, D₃ = det A = 1 > 0
⇒ positive definite ⇒ **minimum** (global, since f is a convex quadratic).

steps.label: Where marks are lost
steps.text:
• Putting the full cross coefficient (−2, −4, 2) off the diagonal instead of half of it.
• Forgetting the minus in f = xᵀAx − bᵀx when reading b.
